title: Order details with customer and product
statement_markdown: Return customer_name, product_name, and quantity for every ordered item by joining customers, orders, order_items, and products. Sort by customer then product.

examples.input: Visible customers, order_items, orders, products tables
examples.explanation: This output comes from the visible sample data.

hints: Follow the foreign-key path from customer to order to item to product.
Give the two name columns clear aliases and use two ORDER BY keys.
explanation: Each JOIN adds information along the relationship chain: customer owns order, order owns item, and item references product. A common mistake is joining product directly to order. Clear aliases prevent ambiguous name columns. Starting at order_items can be an equally valid join order.
reference_solution: SELECT c.name AS customer_name, p.name AS product_name, oi.quantity FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id ORDER BY c.name, p.name

validation.setup_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR(50)); CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR(50), price INT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE); CREATE TABLE order_items (id INT, order_id INT, product_id INT, quantity INT); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Bob'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1, 'P1', 10), (2, 'P2', 20), (3, 'P3', 30); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 1, '2026-01-01'), (2, 2, '2026-01-02'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1, 1, 1, 2), (2, 1, 2, 1), (3, 2, 3, 5);
